method_notes: Tower Hamlets oversubscription criteria for community schools (Starting Primary School in Tower Hamlets 2027 prospectus, 'Oversubscription criteria and tie-break', p16): EHCP first; then 1 looked-after/previously looked-after, 2 medical/social, 3 in-catchment siblings, 4 children of staff, 5 in-catchment children for whom it is their nearest community school in the catchment, 6 other in-catchment, 7 out-of-catchment siblings, 8 others. Tie-break within criteria 3-8: shortest walking distance, measured with a digital Ordnance Survey map from the centre point of the address to the centre point of the school's designated main entrance along the centre line of the shortest approved route (local footpaths and public walkways, with regard to safety; ignores crossing points); equal distances by random allocation. Six catchment areas (Stepney, Bow, Poplar, Isle of Dogs, Wapping, Bethnal Green). The council's 'tie-break cut off distance' is the walking distance of the last child offered, within whichever criterion places ran out, so it is not a simple radius: in-catchment applicants beat closer out-of-catchment ones. Academies that delegate admissions to the LA and use these criteria: Culloden, Old Ford, Solebay (Paradigm), Bygrove, Mulberry Canon Barnett, Mulberry Wood Wharf, Stebon, St Paul's Way Trust, The Clara Grant (prospectus p15). VA/faith schools, Canary Wharf College and Sir William Burrough have their own arrangements.

gaps: Council publishes cut-offs only for oversubscribed schools using the LA criteria (11 in 2026, 14 in 2025, 15 in 2024). Other LA-criteria schools are recorded as all_offered, on the council's statement that an unlisted school offered every applicant a place (or they got a higher preference). Own-admission-authority schools (13 VA/faith schools, 2 Catholic academies, Canary Wharf College x2, Sir William Burrough) have no published figures: not_published, with a note when the council listed them as having places remaining. 2026 sources conflict: the council web page and the 2027 prospectus summary differ for Bigland Green (537 vs 351 m) and Mulberry Wood Wharf (2531 vs 518 m) - web values used, both noted; the prospectus omits Bangabandhu, Bonner (both sites) and Seven Mills, and adds Malmesbury (2473 m, total offered 90 on PAN 60) which the web page lists as having places remaining - Malmesbury recorded from the prospectus with a warning. Prospectus also prints Thomas Buxton total offered 30 (web: 60). Oddities kept as printed: Virginia 2025 cut-off 30 m; Marion Richardson 2025 total offered 90 on PAN 60. 2025 and 2024 figures came from Wayback Machine snapshots of the council page (the live page now shows 2026 only). Columbia, Cyril Jackson, Hermitage and Virginia are academies with catchments and appear in council tables but are not in the prospectus's delegated list; assumed to use the LA method. Cut-offs are within the last criterion reached (catchment-based), so they are not comparable with simple distance radii. PAN = Sept 2027 admission number from the prospectus (some marked as varying; earlier years' PANs differ, e.g. Bonner sites 30 each in 2026). Junior schools (Blue Gate Fields Junior, Lawdale Junior) excluded. Postcodes from GIAS except Bonner Mile End site (E3 4QE, from the prospectus).
